t: Kennington Common was once a swathe of open common land, mostly in Lambeth. It was one of the earliest venues for cricket around London, with matches played between 1724 and 1785. It was also used for fairs, public gatherings and public executions, and important orators addressed crowds here numbering tens of thousands. Two men connected with the Jacobite rising of 1745 died here in 1746. Francis Towneley was an English Catholic supporter of the exiled House of Stuart, executed for his role in the rebellion. David Morgan was a Welsh barrister and Jacobite campaigner.
